_comment: De-brand strangler MOVE-11 (ADR-0562 §8 Fork 2): home the rung-0 kuberos framekernel from cloud/cloud-kernel/crates into the kernel/ META directory. STATUS: AUTHORED BUT NOT EXECUTABLE — this plan encodes the correct destination shape, face assignment, and de-brand map, but the block is BLOCKED on three mechanical defects proven by dry-run (see `_blockers`). It is committed as the settled design so the unblocking lane does not have to re-derive it; `oya-reorg-codemod dry-run` fail-closes on it TODAY and must keep fail-closing until the blockers are cleared. Faces on evidence: 1 -> kernel/ports (hal-kernel declares 17 public traits — Arch/MemoryApi/InterruptApi/TimerApi/ConsoleWrite/Sealed plus the sealed cpu/irq/mm/smp/time/virtio/confidential capability set — and its implementors live in a DIFFERENT crate: arch-aarch64-adapter/src/hal_caps.rs carries real `impl hal::sealed::Sealed`/`impl hal::<trait> for Aarch64*` blocks, and arch-x86-64-adapter does the same. That cross-crate implementor seam is exactly the condition os-move-plan found ABSENT for cloud-os proto-api — there every implementor of the seven public traits lived inside proto-api itself, so it was core; here the seam is real, so hal is ports); 2 -> kernel/adapters (the arch-aarch64 / arch-x86-64 backends are the hardware-specific implementors of that ports seam, one per ISA, selected by an optional feature on the composition binary — the textbook adapter shape); 4 -> kernel/core (frame-kernel is the safe Frame engine layered over the HAL seam; ksync-kernel is no_std concurrency primitives with no trait seam, consumed by both adapters; user-layout-kernel is arch-neutral pure EL0 layout math with ZERO dependencies and 75 host tests; app is the composition binary that produces the bare-metal image — core and NOT facade on the same reasoning os-move-plan applied to init-app: a kernel image is not a sold multi-tenant surface, so it carries no facade face). The 13 excluded crates (the aarch64 tests-host harness + the 12 freestanding ring-3/EL0 user programs) are deliberately NOT listed as moves: every one is physically nested inside an adapter crate dir and rides along with its parent under codemod step 7, which is REQUIRED rather than incidental — tests-host reaches its subject via `include!("../../../<crate>/src/*.rs")` and the user programs are embedded by `include_bytes!` against a workspace-root-relative `out/`, so promoting them to independent moves would break the relative couplings that keep them working. De-brand per ADR-0532/0533: oya-cloud-kernel-<tail> -> kernel-<tail>, matching the kernel-asterinas-* crates already landed at this destination by ADR-0611.

_blockers._comment: Each blocker is mechanical and was proven, not inferred. Until all three clear, this plan must not be applied. The destination `kernel/` is NOT empty: ADR-0611 (Proposed 2026-07-04, landed on dev) populated it with kernel/core/asterinas-boundary + kernel/harness/asterinas-real-boot, and ADR-0611 §Decision explicitly describes cloud/cloud-kernel as the nested-workspace PRECEDENT it mirrors — i.e. a parallel workspace, not a tree kernel/ was expecting to absorb. ADR-0562 §8 Fork 2 was written when kernel/ was still empty.
_blockers.B1_destination_occupied_by_an_incompatib: kernel/ is already a nested Cargo workspace root (kernel/Cargo.toml, kernel/Cargo.lock, kernel/OWNERS) and cloud/cloud-kernel is another one. Landing the kuberos crates into kernel/'s faces requires ONE workspace at kernel/, but the two sides need opposite values of three single-valued per-tree files: (a) [workspace.package] — kuberos is edition 2021 / rust-version 1.85, asterinas is edition 2024 / rust-version 1.97.1, and both sides inherit via `.workspace = true`; (b) .cargo/config.toml — kuberos needs `[build] target = aarch64-unknown-none-softfloat` plus `[unstable] build-std`, while kernel-asterinas-real-boot is a std host crate depending on reqwest+rustls and cannot compile for a bare-metal no-std target; (c) rust-toolchain.toml — kuberos pins nightly-2026-02-28 (build-std is nightly-only and needs rust-src), asterinas is stable 1.97.1. (b) and (c) are unresolvable by editing: Cargo resolves both files by walking up from the invocation directory, so one tree cannot carry two values. (a) is resolvable only by de-inheriting edition/rust-version in 7 manifests, which is a REFACTOR, not a MOVE.
_blockers.B2_codemod_does_not_rewrite_workspace_de: cloud/cloud-kernel/Cargo.toml expresses 5 of its 7 internal edges in [workspace.dependencies] as path deps (hal, frame, arch-aarch64, arch-x86_64, user_layout -> `path = "crates/oya-cloud-kernel-*"`). The codemod's cargo::rewrite_dep_tables_recursive walks only DEP_TABLES = [dependencies, dev-dependencies, build-dependencies] and recurses only into [target.<cfg>]; its own comment says it deliberately avoids recursing into [package]/[workspace]. So all 5 path deps would be left pointing at the vacated crates/ directory and the nested workspace would break SILENTLY — the codemod reports success. Fixing this is a change to the codemod, not to this plan.
_blockers.B3_path_literals_encode_the_old_layout: 33 include!/include_bytes!/include_str! literals under cloud/cloud-kernel/crates traverse UP out of their own crate, and 6 of them name the OLD crate directory outright, e.g. arch-aarch64-adapter/tests-host/src/lib.rs does `include!("../../../oya-cloud-kernel-user-layout-kernel/src/layout.rs")`. The flat `crates/<crate>` layout becomes the two-level `<face>/<crate>` layout, so BOTH the directory name and the number of `../` hops change (the correct post-move path is `../../../../core/user-layout/src/layout.rs`). The codemod's rust_src module rewrites snake-case crate identifiers only and documents that assumption explicitly — 'the crate-ident rename class, which is the only Rust-source change a path move induces'. That assumption does not hold for this block, so these 33 literals would dangle.
